name: Transposition of the Great Arteries and Conotruncal Cardiac Anomaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for TGA with Conotruncal Anomalies

criteria.description: Anatomical confirmation of ventriculoarterial discordance with aorta arising from right ventricle and pulmonary artery from left ventricle
Presence of conotruncal cardiac anomalies such as ventricular septal defect, pulmonary stenosis, or overriding aorta
Clinical evidence of central cyanosis in neonatal period
Echocardiographic visualization of great artery transposition and associated conotruncal defects

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Anatomical confirmation of ventriculoarterial discordance with associated conotruncal malformation on echocardiography
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging and clinical presentation in the neonatal period.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Central cyanosis due to systemic desaturation
pathognomonic.notes: Typically presents within hours to days after birth
searchTerms: central cyanosis due to low blood oxygen
heart artery and ventricle mismatch on scan

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congestive heart failure signs in neonate
pathognomonic.notes: Includes tachypnea, hepatomegaly, and poor feeding

common.symptomName: Tachypnea due to pulmonary overcirculation or hypoxia
searchTerms: fast breathing from lung blood overload
rapid breathing due to low oxygen

common.symptomName: Poor feeding and failure to thrive
searchTerms: difficulty feeding and not gaining weight
failure to thrive with feeding problems

common.symptomName: Murmur due to associated ventricular septal defect or pulmonary stenosis
searchTerms: heart murmur from hole or valve narrowing
murmur due to ventricular defect or stenosis
abnormal heart sound from heart defects

common.symptomName: Clubbing of fingers (in older infants if untreated)

searchTerms: high red blood cell count from low oxygen
increased blood thickness due to low oxygen

occasional.symptomName: Hepatomegaly due to right heart failure
searchTerms: enlarged liver from right heart failure

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits due to hypoxic-ischemic injury
searchTerms: nerve deficits due to lack of oxygen

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment secondary to low cardiac output
searchTerms: kidney problems from poor heart output
renal impairment due to low cardiac output

laboratory: Elevated hematocrit due to secondary polycythemia
Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating ventriculoarterial discordance and conotruncal defects
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular markings
Cardiac MRI or CT angiography for detailed anatomical assessment
genetic: Mutations or deletions in genes associated with conotruncal defects (e.g., 22q11.2 deletion syndrome)
Genetic testing for syndromic associations such as DiGeorge syndrome

distinguishingFeatures: Pulmonary stenosis with overriding aorta and ventricular septal defect
Characteristic boot-shaped heart on chest X-ray
Both great arteries arise predominantly from right ventricle
Often associated with large ventricular septal defect

redFlags: Severe central cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
Rapid clinical deterioration requiring urgent surgical intervention
references: Anderson RH, et al. Paediatric Cardiology. 4th Edition. 2019.
Maron BJ, et al. Braunwald's Heart Disease. 11th Edition. 2019.
